title: Provider-Agnostic Service Auth And Deploy Adapter Framework
specification:
# PRD: Provider-Agnostic Service Auth And Deploy Adapter Framework

Priority: high

## Problem
`autonomy-v2` can run generic deploy commands today, but it has no provider-agnostic way to authenticate external services, no connection model to track which service/account a deploy should use, and no secure framework for mapping dynamic local env secrets back into the control-plane UI. Without this layer, every new deploy target such as Netlify or Heroku becomes a one-off core-code change or an unsafe ad hoc secret convention.

## Goal
Add a control-plane and bridge framework for provider-agnostic service connections, local secret resolution, auth verification, and deploy adapter execution so new services can be integrated through a shared contract instead of custom deploy logic in core flows.

## Requirements
- Add a provider-agnostic service connection model with fields for provider id, connection id, auth strategy, status, last verified time, non-secret account metadata, failure classification, and optional capability metadata.
- Add new control-plane job types for service auth lifecycle and execution, including start, complete, verify/test, and deploy flows that can carry provider and connection context instead of only `repoId`.
- Keep the local bridge as the trust boundary for obtaining, resolving, validating, and using provider credentials; the hosted control plane must not persist or expose raw secret values in status, prompts, or chat.
- Support dynamic local env alias mapping so providers can declare logical secret fields such as `apiToken`, `siteId`, or `appName`, and each connection can map those fields to arbitrary local env keys loaded from approved env sources.
- Use existing env-loading behavior as the execution source of truth, but formalize precedence so runtime-injected env remains preferred, machine-local env files remain acceptable for secrets, and shared env files are treated cautiously.
- Add a provider adapter contract that declares supported auth strategies, required logical fields, required scopes, verification behavior, deploy command construction, optional preflight checks, and optional post-deploy metadata reporting.
- Make provider hookup primarily config-driven after the framework exists, so supported providers can be registered through descriptors and adapter commands without adding new core deploy branching for each provider.
- Expose connection state in the control-plane UI with secret-safe statuses such as connected, verification failed, expired, revoked, insufficient scopes, or needs reconnect, along with non-secret labels like account, team, app, or site name when available.
- Support a manual token-based setup path as an initial fallback, but model the framework so browser/device/OAuth-style flows can also be supported through the same connection lifecycle without redesigning the core contract.
- Ensure deploy execution can select a provider connection explicitly and inject resolved secret material only at command execution time.
- Add focused tests for connection lifecycle state, env alias resolution, secret-safe status reporting, bridge execution payloads, deploy adapter invocation, and failure classification.
- Do not require live GitHub PR inspection for this PRD; current GitHub validation is unavailable in repo status and should not be treated as a dependency for the service-auth framework.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A repo can define one or more provider connections with stable `connectionId` values and secret-safe status metadata visible in the control plane.
- Service-auth and deploy jobs carry provider and connection context through validation, queueing, bridge execution, and status updates without relying on ad hoc payload fields.
- The bridge can resolve provider-declared logical secret fields from dynamically named env keys and inject them into execution without exposing raw values in logs, status payloads, or chat context.
- A provider adapter can be registered through the shared contract and can declare auth requirements, verification behavior, and deploy command construction without adding a new hardcoded deploy branch in core flow.
- The UI can show whether each required logical field resolves successfully for a connection without displaying the underlying env value.
- Manual token-based connection setup can mark a connection verified only after bridge-side validation succeeds.
- The framework can support future Netlify-like and Heroku-like providers through configuration plus adapter descriptors, without additional redesign of the core auth/deploy model.
- Existing generic deploy behavior continues to work for repos that do not opt into provider-backed connections.
- Tests cover successful connection verification, missing env alias, unresolved secret field, invalid credential, insufficient scope, deploy execution with resolved secrets, and secret-safe status rendering.

## Verification
- Run `npm run typecheck`.
- Run focused unit tests for control-plane connection state, bridge job handling, env alias resolution, and deploy adapter execution.
- Run relevant control-plane and deploy smoke tests if shared job contracts or served UI/API behavior change.
- Confirm repo status and manager UI show connection metadata and failure classes without exposing raw secret values.
- Confirm a provider-backed deploy path receives resolved execution env only at runtime and that a non-provider deploy path still behaves as before.
